docs.title: Open AXI Interconnect
docs.text:
Welcome to the Open AXI Interconnect documentation — a fully synthesizable, parameterizable AXI4/AXI4-Lite crossbar interconnect for FPGA and ASIC designs.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• AXI4/AXI4-Lite Support: Full crossbar interconnect with configurable master/slave counts
  • Parameterizable: Data width, address width, and ID width are all configurable
  • Synthesizable: Clean SystemVerilog RTL targeting both FPGA and ASIC flows
  • Well-Verified: Comprehensive cocotb testbench with functional coverage
  • Open Source: MIT licensed — free for commercial and academic use

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Open AXI4 RTL Subsystem is a lightweight, synthesizable AMBA AXI4-Lite based system-on-chip building block. It is intended for FPGA and ASIC designs that need a simple memory-mapped interconnect with a small set of peripherals.

docs.title: 1. AXI4-Lite Interconnect (axi_lite_interconnect)
docs.text:
The interconnect implements a single-master, multi-slave address decoder and router:

  • Receives AXI4-Lite transactions from the master.
  • Decodes the 32-bit address against the fixed memory map.
  • Routes AW/W/B and AR/R signals to the selected slave.
  • Returns the slave response to the master.

Current limitations (by design in this version):

  • Single master only.
  • No pipelining / no outstanding transactions.
  • No burst support (AXI4-Lite only).

docs.title: 2. AXI4-Lite Slave Template (axi_lite_slave)
docs.text: A generic 4-register AXI4-Lite slave used as a reference implementation. It supports byte-wise writes via WSTRB.

docs.title: RAM (ram)
docs.text:
• 4 KB memory array (1024 x 32-bit words).
  • Exposes control, status, address, and data registers at offsets 0x00-0x0C.
  • Writes to the data register store into the memory array at the address register value.

docs.title: UART (uart)
docs.text:
• Minimal UART model with control, status, TX data, and RX data registers.
  • Status bit 0 indicates TX ready.
  • TX data is captured but not serialized in this version.

docs.title: Timer (timer)
docs.text:
• Free-running 32-bit counter.
  • Compare register for interrupt generation.
  • Control bits: enable, reset.
  • irq is asserted when enabled and count >= compare.

docs.title: GPIO (gpio)
docs.text:
• 32 bidirectional GPIO pins.
  • Direction register: 1 = output, 0 = input (high-Z).
  • Output and input value registers.

docs.title: 4. Top-Level (axi_subsystem)
docs.text: Instantiates the interconnect and all four peripherals, exposing a single AXI4-Lite master interface plus external peripheral pins.

docs.title: Address Map
docs.text: See docs/memory_map.md and docs/register_map.md for detailed register-level descriptions.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
• Cocotb tests: verification/cocotb/test_axi_lite.py
  • SystemVerilog testbench: verification/sv/tb_axi_lite.sv
  • SystemVerilog assertions: verification/assertions/axi_assertions.sv

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• In this minimal subsystem, AWREADY/WREADY/ARREADY are tied high, so the master can generally complete the address/data phase in one clock cycle.
  • BVALID and RVALID are asserted one cycle after the request is accepted and remain asserted until the corresponding BREADY/RREADY is seen.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
This document defines the memory map of the AXI4-Lite subsystem.

The subsystem implements a memory-mapped architecture where each peripheral is assigned a unique address range. The AXI master accesses peripherals using read and write transactions.

Architecture:

             AXI Master
                 |
                 |
          AXI4-Lite Interconnect
                 |
   +-------------+-------------+-------------+
   |             |             |             |
  RAM          UART          Timer         GPIO

docs.title: 2. Address Space
docs.text:
The AXI subsystem uses a 32-bit address space.

Peripheral Base Address End Address Size RAM 0x0000_0000 0x0000_FFFF 64 KB UART 0x4000_0000 0x4000_0FFF 4 KB Timer 0x4001_0000 0x4001_0FFF 4 KB GPIO 0x4002_0000 0x4002_0FFF 4 KB

docs.title: 3. AXI Address Decoding
docs.text:
The interconnect is responsible for:

  1. Receiving AXI requests from the master.
  2. Comparing the address against peripheral ranges.
  3. Routing the transaction to the correct slave.
  4. Returning the response to the master.

Example:

Address = 0x40000010
0x40000000 - 0x40000FFF
        |
        v
      UART

docs.title: 4. Supported Transactions
docs.text:
Version 1:

Supported:

  • Single beat reads
  • Single beat writes
  • 32-bit data width
  • Write strobes (WSTRB)

Not supported:

  • Bursts
  • Multiple outstanding transactions
  • AXI IDs
  • Cache attributes

docs.title: Write UART Data
docs.text:
Master writes:

Address: 0x40000008
Data:    0x00000041
Operation: Transmit character 'A'

docs.title: Read Timer Counter
docs.text:
Master reads:
Address: 0x40010008
Response: Current timer value

docs.title: Write GPIO Output
docs.text:
Master writes:
Address: 0x40020004
Data:    0xA5A5A5A5
Operation: Drive GPIO output value

docs.title: 1. Register Conventions
docs.text:
All registers:

  • Width: 32 bits
  • Access size: 32 bits
  • Reset value: defined per register
  • Address offset relative to peripheral base address

Access types:

Type Meaning RW Read and Write RO Read Only WO Write Only

docs.title: 2. RAM Controller
docs.text:
Base Address: 0x0000_0000

The RAM peripheral provides simple memory storage.

docs.title: Register Map
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 CONTROL RW Enable RAM 0x04 STATUS RO RAM status (READY=1) 0x08 ADDRESS RW Memory address pointer 0x0C DATA RW Read/write data at ADDRESS

docs.title: CONTROL Register
docs.text:
Bit Name Access Description 0 ENABLE RW Enable RAM

Reset: 0x0000_0000

docs.title: STATUS Register
docs.text:
Bit Name Access Description 0 READY RO RAM ready

Reset: 0x0000_0001

docs.title: 3. UART Peripheral
docs.text:
Base Address: 0x4000_0000

Provides serial communication through AXI transactions.

docs.title: Register Map
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 CTRL RW UART configuration 0x04 STATUS RO UART state 0x08 TX_DATA WO Transmit byte 0x0C RX_DATA RO Received byte

docs.title: CTRL Register
docs.text:
Bit Name Description 0 ENABLE Enable UART 1 TX_ENABLE Enable transmitter 2 RX_ENABLE Enable receiver

Reset: 0x0000_0000

docs.title: STATUS Register
docs.text:
Bit Name Description 0 TX_READY Transmit available 1 RX_VALID Received data available

Reset: 0x0000_0001 (TX_READY set)

docs.title: 4. Timer Peripheral
docs.text:
Base Address: 0x4001_0000

Generates timing information and interrupts.

docs.title: Register Map
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 CTRL RW Timer control 0x04 STATUS RO Timer state 0x08 COUNT RO Current counter 0x0C COMPARE RW Interrupt compare value

docs.title: CTRL Register
docs.text: Bit Name Description 0 ENABLE Enable counting 1 RESET Reset counter to zero

docs.title: STATUS Register
docs.text: Bit Name Description 0 ACTIVE Timer is enabled

docs.title: 5. GPIO Peripheral
docs.text:
Base Address: 0x4002_0000

General purpose input/output.

docs.title: Register Map
docs.text: Offset Register Access Description 0x00 DIR RW Pin direction (1=output, 0=input) 0x04 OUT RW Output value 0x08 IN RO Input value

docs.title: UART transmit
docs.text:
1. Enable UART: WRITE UART_CTRL, ENABLE=1
  2. Check status: READ UART_STATUS until TX_READY==1
  3. Send byte: WRITE UART_TX_DATA

docs.title: Timer usage
docs.text:
1. Configure compare value: WRITE TIMER_COMPARE
  2. Enable timer: WRITE TIMER_CTRL, ENABLE=1
  3. Poll status or connect irq to interrupt controller.

docs.title: GPIO usage
docs.text:
1. Configure direction: WRITE GPIO_DIR
  2. Set output: WRITE GPIO_OUT
  3. Read input: READ GPIO_IN

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect is a lightweight, synthesizable AMBA AXI4-Lite based system-on-chip building block. It is intended for FPGA and ASIC designs that need a simple memory-mapped interconnect with a small set of peripherals.

docs.title: Key Components
docs.text: Component Description AXI4-Lite Interconnect Single-master, multi-slave address decoder and router RAM 4 KB memory array with control/status registers UART Minimal UART with TX/RX data registers Timer Free-running 32-bit counter with compare interrupt GPIO 32 bidirectional pins with direction control

docs.title: Design Characteristics
docs.text:
• Single master only — one AXI4-Lite master interface
  • No pipelining — no outstanding transactions
  • No burst support — AXI4-Lite only (single-beat)
  • Fixed address map — peripherals at hardcoded base addresses
  • Configurable parameters — data width, address width

docs.title: Address Map Summary
docs.text: Peripheral Base Address End Address Size RAM 0x0000_0000 0x0000_FFFF 64 KB UART 0x4000_0000 0x4000_0FFF 4 KB Timer 0x4001_0000 0x4001_0FFF 4 KB GPIO 0x4002_0000 0x4002_0FFF 4 KB

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Default Description ADDR_WIDTH 32 Address bus width in bits DATA_WIDTH 32 Data bus width in bits NUM_SLAVES 4 Number of slave peripherals

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Protocol Compliance
docs.text: This page documents how the Open AXI Interconnect implements the AMBA AXI4-Lite protocol.

docs.title: Protocol Overview
docs.text:
AXI4-Lite is a lightweight subset of the full AXI4 protocol designed for simple control register access. It supports:

  • Single-beat transactions only (no bursts)
  • Fixed data width (32-bit in this design)
  • No cache, protection, or QoS signals
  • No exclusive access or locked transactions

docs.title: Write Address Channel (AW)
docs.text: Signal Width Direction Description AWVALID 1 Master → Slave Address/control valid AWREADY 1 Slave → Master Slave ready to accept address AWADDR 32 Master → Slave Write address AWPROT 3 Master → Slave Protection type (unused)

docs.title: Write Data Channel (W)
docs.text: Signal Width Direction Description WVALID 1 Master → Slave Write data valid WREADY 1 Slave → Master Slave ready to accept data WDATA 32 Master → Slave Write data WSTRB 4 Master → Slave Write strobe (byte-wise enable)

docs.title: Write Response Channel (B)
docs.text: Signal Width Direction Description BVALID 1 Slave → Master Response valid BREADY 1 Master → Slave Master ready to accept response BRESP 2 Slave → Master Response status (00 = OKAY)

docs.title: Read Address Channel (AR)
docs.text: Signal Width Direction Description ARVALID 1 Master → Slave Address/control valid ARREADY 1 Slave → Master Slave ready to accept address ARADDR 32 Master → Slave Read address ARPROT 3 Master → Slave Protection type (unused)

docs.title: Read Data Channel (R)
docs.text: Signal Width Direction Description RVALID 1 Slave → Master Read data valid RREADY 1 Master → Slave Master ready to accept data RDATA 32 Slave → Master Read data RRESP 2 Slave → Master Response status (00 = OKAY)

docs.title: Handshake Rules
docs.text:
1. Source must not wait for READY before asserting VALID
  2. Destination can wait for VALID before asserting READY
  3. Once VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs
  4. READY can be asserted before or after VALID

docs.title: Response Codes
docs.text:
Code Name Description 00 OKAY Normal access success 01 EXOKAY Exclusive access okay (not used in AXI4-Lite) 10 SLVERR Slave error — access reached slave but slave returned error 11 DECERR Decode error — no slave at the requested address

Current Implementation

All responses in this design return OKAY (00). SLVERR and DECERR are not yet implemented.

docs.title: Write Strobe (WSTRB)
docs.text:
WSTRB controls which bytes of WDATA are written:

WSTRB Bytes Written 0001 Byte 0 only 0010 Byte 1 only 0100 Byte 2 only 1000 Byte 3 only 0011 Bytes 0-1 1100 Bytes 2-3 1111 All bytes

The slave template (axi_lite_slave) implements byte-wise writes using:

if (WSTRB[0]) reg_data[7:0]   <= WDATA[7:0];
if (WSTRB[1]) reg_data[15:8]  <= WDATA[15:8];
if (WSTRB[2]) reg_data[23:16] <= WDATA[23:16];
if (WSTRB[3]) reg_data[31:24] <= WDATA[31:24];

docs.title: FSM Diagrams
docs.text: This page documents the finite state machines used in the AXI4-Lite interconnect and slave peripherals.

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Write Transaction FSM
docs.text:
The write transaction follows the AXI4-Lite handshake protocol across two channels: Write Address (AW) and Write Data (W). The response is returned on the Write Response (B) channel.

┌──────────┐    AWVALID & AWREADY    ┌──────────┐
│   IDLE   │ ───────────────────────▶ │ AW_ADDR  │
└──────────┘                          └────┬─────┘
      ▲                                      │
      │                                      │ WVALID & WREADY
      │                                      ▼
      │                               ┌──────────┐
      │                               │  W_DATA  │
      │                               └────┬─────┘
      │                                      │
      │                                      │ BVALID & BREADY
      │                                      ▼
      │                               ┌──────────┐
      └───────────────────────────────│   DONE   │
                                      └──────────┘

docs.title: State Descriptions
docs.text: State Description IDLE Waiting for a new write transaction. Sample AWVALID and WVALID. AW_ADDR Address accepted (AWREADY asserted). Wait for write data. W_DATA Write data accepted (WREADY asserted). Prepare response. DONE Response valid (BVALID asserted). Return to IDLE on BREADY.

docs.title: State Transition Table
docs.text:
Current Condition Next IDLE AWVALID && AWREADY AW_ADDR AW_ADDR WVALID && WREADY W_DATA W_DATA — DONE DONE BREADY IDLE

Combined AW/W

In AXI4-Lite, the address and data can arrive in any order. The slave must accept both before issuing a response.

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Read Transaction FSM
docs.text:
The read transaction uses the Read Address (AR) channel and returns data on the Read Data (R) channel.

┌──────────┐    ARVALID & ARREADY    ┌──────────┐
│   IDLE   │ ───────────────────────▶ │ AR_ADDR  │
└──────────┘                          └────┬─────┘
      ▲                                  │
      │                                  │ Data ready
      │                                  ▼
      │                           ┌──────────┐
      │                           │ R_DATA   │
      │                           └────┬─────┘
      │                                  │
      │                                  │ RVALID & RREADY
      │                                  ▼
      │                           ┌──────────┐
      └───────────────────────────│   DONE   │
                                  └──────────┘

docs.title: State Descriptions
docs.text: State Description IDLE Waiting for a new read transaction. Sample ARVALID. AR_ADDR Address accepted (ARREADY asserted). Fetch data from register/memory. R_DATA Data valid (RVALID asserted). Return to IDLE on RREADY. DONE Transaction complete. Return to IDLE.

docs.title: State Transition Table
docs.text: Current Condition Next IDLE ARVALID && ARREADY AR_ADDR AR_ADDR Data fetched R_DATA R_DATA RVALID && RREADY DONE DONE — IDLE

docs.title: Timer Counter FSM
docs.text:
The timer has a simple two-state counter with a reset control.

┌──────────┐    CTRL.RESET=1    ┌──────────┐
│  COUNT   │ ─────────────────▶ │  CLEAR   │
└────┬─────┘                    └────┬─────┘
     │                              │
     │ CTRL.ENABLE=1                │ CTRL.RESET=0
     │ (increment)                  │ (next cycle)
     └──────────────────────────────┘
State Description COUNT Counter increments by 1 each clock cycle when ENABLE=1. CLEAR Counter resets to 0. Returns to COUNT on next cycle if RESET is deasserted.

docs.title: UART TX FSM
docs.text:
The UART transmitter is a placeholder in this version. The conceptual FSM would be:

┌──────────┐    TX_ENABLE=1    ┌──────────┐
│   IDLE   │ ─────────────────▶ │  LOAD    │
└────┬─────┘                    └────┬─────┘
     │                              │
     │ TX_DONE                      │
     │                              │
     └──────────────────────────────┘
State Description IDLE Waiting for TX_ENABLE. LOAD Load TX_DATA into shift register. SHIFT Shift out bits (not implemented in this version).

Placeholder

The current UART implementation does not include a baud-rate generator or bit-shifting logic. It is a register-only model suitable for basic software bring-up.

docs.title: Memory Map
docs.text: This page documents the complete address space of the Open AXI Interconnect subsystem.

docs.title: Decode Logic
docs.text:
The interconnect uses the following decode function (from rtl/axi/axi_lite_interconnect.sv):

localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] RAM_END    = 32'h0000_FFFF;
localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] UART_BASE  = 32'h4000_0000;
localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] UART_END   = 32'h4000_0FFF;
localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] TIMER_BASE = 32'h4001_0000;
localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] TIMER_END  = 32'h4001_0FFF;
localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] GPIO_BASE  = 32'h4002_0000;
localparam [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] GPIO_END   = 32'h4002_0FFF;

function automatic slave_sel_t decode(input [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] addr);
    if      ((addr >= UART_BASE)  && (addr <= UART_END))  decode = SLAVE_UART;
    else if ((addr >= TIMER_BASE) && (addr <= TIMER_END)) decode = SLAVE_TIMER;
    else if ((addr >= GPIO_BASE)  && (addr <= GPIO_END))  decode = SLAVE_GPIO;
    else                                                   decode = SLAVE_RAM;
endfunction

RAM catch-all

Any address not explicitly matching UART, Timer, or GPIO is routed to RAM. This includes addresses above 0x4003_0000 and the gap between 0x0001_0000 and 0x3FFF_FFFF.

docs.title: Peripheral Base Addresses
docs.text: Peripheral Base Address End Address Size Slave Index RAM 0x0000_0000 0x0000_FFFF 64 KB 0 UART 0x4000_0000 0x4000_0FFF 4 KB 1 Timer 0x4001_0000 0x4001_0FFF 4 KB 2 GPIO 0x4002_0000 0x4002_0FFF 4 KB 3

docs.title: Python Constants (for cocotb tests)
docs.text:
RAM_BASE   = 0x0000_0000
UART_BASE  = 0x4000_0000
TIMER_BASE = 0x4001_0000
GPIO_BASE  = 0x4002_0000

These constants are defined in verification/cocotb/test_axi_lite.py and must match the RTL decode logic.

docs.title: Detailed Architecture Overview
docs.text: This page provides an in-depth look at each component in the Open AXI Interconnect subsystem.

docs.title: 1. AXI4-Lite Interconnect (axi_lite_interconnect)
docs.text: The interconnect is the central routing fabric. It receives AXI4-Lite transactions from a single master and routes them to the appropriate slave based on the transaction address.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Address decode: Compare the 32-bit address against fixed peripheral ranges
  • Write routing: Drive AW*, W*, and BREADY to the selected slave
  • Read routing: Drive AR* and RREADY to the selected slave
  • Response muxing: Return the selected slave's response to the master

docs.title: Address Decode Function
docs.text:
function automatic slave_sel_t decode(input [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] addr);
    if      ((addr >= UART_BASE)  && (addr <= UART_END))  decode = SLAVE_UART;
    else if ((addr >= TIMER_BASE) && (addr <= TIMER_END)) decode = SLAVE_TIMER;
    else if ((addr >= GPIO_BASE)  && (addr <= GPIO_END))  decode = SLAVE_GPIO;
    else                                                   decode = SLAVE_RAM;
endfunction

RAM as default

Any address not matching UART, Timer, or GPIO ranges falls through to RAM. This means RAM effectively occupies the entire lower 64 KB and all unmapped upper addresses.

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text: Limitation Reason Single master only Simplifies arbitration — none needed No outstanding transactions Simplifies response tracking No burst support AXI4-Lite protocol restriction Fixed memory map Hardcoded for this subsystem version

docs.title: 2. AXI4-Lite Slave Template (axi_lite_slave)
docs.text:
A generic 4-register AXI4-Lite slave used as a reference implementation. It demonstrates:

  • Byte-wise writes via WSTRB
  • Separate read/write state machines
  • Register banking with reset values

docs.title: Register Layout
docs.text: Offset Register Reset Value Description 0x00 CONTROL 0x0000_0000 User control bits 0x04 STATUS 0xDEAD_BEEF User status bits 0x08 DATA 0x0000_0000 General-purpose data 0x0C VERSION 0x0000_0001 IP version register

docs.title: RAM (ram)
docs.text:
• 4 KB memory array (1024 × 32-bit words)
  • Control register (0x00): ENABLE bit
  • Status register (0x04): READY flag
  • Address register (0x08): Memory address pointer
  • Data register (0x0C): Read/write data at the address pointer

Writes to the data register store into mem[address]. Reads from the data register return mem[address].

docs.title: UART (uart)
docs.text:
• Minimal UART model with no actual serialization
  • CTRL register (0x00): ENABLE, TX_ENABLE, RX_ENABLE
  • STATUS register (0x04): TX_READY, RX_VALID
  • TX_DATA (0x08): Write-only transmit byte
  • RX_DATA (0x0C): Read-only received byte

In this version, tx is a placeholder line driven from CTRL[0] ? tx_data[0] : 1'b1.

docs.title: Timer (timer)
docs.text:
• Free-running 32-bit counter
  • CTRL register (0x00): ENABLE (bit 0), RESET (bit 1)
  • COUNT register (0x08): Current counter value (read-only)
  • COMPARE register (0x0C): Interrupt threshold
  • irq output: Asserted when ENABLE==1 and COUNT >= COMPARE

When RESET is set, the counter clears to zero on the next clock edge.

docs.title: GPIO (gpio)
docs.text:
• 32 bidirectional pins
  • DIR register (0x00): 1 = output, 0 = input (high-Z)
  • OUT register (0x04): Output drive value
  • IN register (0x08): Sampled pin value (read-only)

Tristate implementation: 

assign gpio_pins[i] = reg_dir[i] ? reg_out[i] : 1'bz;
assign reg_in[i]    = gpio_pins[i];

docs.title: 4. Top-Level (axi_subsystem)
docs.text:
The top-level module instantiates:

  1. axi_lite_interconnect — the routing fabric
  2. ram — slave index 0
  3. uart — slave index 1
  4. timer — slave index 2
  5. gpio — slave index 3

It exposes a single AXI4-Lite master interface plus external peripheral pins (uart_tx, uart_rx, timer_irq, gpio_pins).

docs.title: Parameterization
docs.text:
module axi_subsystem #(
    parameter ADDR_WIDTH = 32,
    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 32
)(
    // ... ports ...
);

All sub-modules inherit these parameters, ensuring consistent bus widths throughout the hierarchy.

docs.title: Register Map
docs.text: This page documents every register in each peripheral, including field-level bit definitions.

docs.title: RAM Registers
docs.text:
Base: 0x0000_0000

Offset Name Access Reset Description 0x00 CONTROL R/W 0x0000_0000 Memory enable 0x04 STATUS R 0x0000_0001 Ready flag 0x08 ADDR R/W 0x0000_0000 Memory address pointer 0x0C DATA R/W 0x0000_0000 Data at ADDR

docs.title: RAM CONTROL (0x00)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [0] ENABLE 1 = memory array active [31:1] — Reserved (read as 0)

docs.title: RAM STATUS (0x04)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [0] READY Always 1 — memory is always ready [31:1] — Reserved

docs.title: RAM ADDR (0x08)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [9:0] ADDR Word address into 1024-entry array [31:10] — Reserved

docs.title: RAM DATA (0x0C)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [31:0] DATA Read/write data at ADDR

docs.title: UART Registers
docs.text:
Base: 0x4000_0000

Offset Name Access Reset Description 0x00 CTRL R/W 0x0000_0000 UART control 0x04 STATUS R 0x0000_0001 UART status 0x08 TX_DATA W 0x0000_0000 Transmit data 0x0C RX_DATA R 0x0000_0000 Receive data

docs.title: UART CTRL (0x00)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [0] ENABLE 1 = UART active [1] TX_ENABLE 1 = TX path enabled [2] RX_ENABLE 1 = RX path enabled [31:3] — Reserved

docs.title: UART STATUS (0x04)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [0] TX_READY 1 = TX buffer empty, ready for next byte [1] RX_VALID 1 = RX data valid [31:2] — Reserved

docs.title: UART TX_DATA (0x08)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [7:0] DATA Byte to transmit [31:8] — Reserved

docs.title: UART RX_DATA (0x0C)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [7:0] DATA Last received byte [31:8] — Reserved

docs.title: Timer Registers
docs.text:
Base: 0x4001_0000

Offset Name Access Reset Description 0x00 CTRL R/W 0x0000_0000 Timer control 0x04 — — — Reserved 0x08 COUNT R 0x0000_0000 Current counter value 0x0C COMPARE R/W 0xFFFF_FFFF Compare threshold

docs.title: Timer CTRL (0x00)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [0] ENABLE 1 = counter increments every clock [1] RESET 1 = clear counter to zero on next clock [31:2] — Reserved

docs.title: Timer COUNT (0x08)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [31:0] COUNT Current 32-bit counter value

docs.title: Timer COMPARE (0x0C)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [31:0] COMPARE Threshold for timer_irq assertion

docs.title: GPIO Registers
docs.text:
Base: 0x4002_0000

Offset Name Access Reset Description 0x00 DIR R/W 0x0000_0000 Pin direction 0x04 OUT R/W 0x0000_0000 Output drive value 0x08 IN R 0x0000_0000 Sampled pin value

docs.title: GPIO DIR (0x00)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [31:0] DIR 1 = output, 0 = input (high-Z)

docs.title: GPIO OUT (0x04)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [31:0] OUT Value driven when pin is output

docs.title: GPIO IN (0x08)
docs.text: Bit Field Description [31:0] IN Current sampled pin value

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Complete installation guide for the Open AXI Interconnect development environment.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Linux or macOS (Windows with WSL2 supported)
  • 4 GB RAM minimum (8 GB recommended)
  • 2 GB free disk space

docs.title: Step 1: Install Python
docs.text:
Ensure Python 3.8 or newer is installed:

python3 --version

If not installed, download from python.org or use your package manager.

docs.title: Step 2: Install Verilator
docs.text:
Ubuntu/DebianmacOSFrom Source 
sudo apt-get install verilator

brew install verilator

git clone https://github.com/verilator/verilator
cd verilator
autoconf
./configure
make -j$(nproc)
sudo make install

docs.title: Step 3: Install Python Dependencies
docs.text:
pip install -r requirements.txt

This installs:

  • cocotb — Python testbench framework
  • cocotb-bus — Bus functional models
  • pytest — Unit testing framework

docs.title: Step 4: Verify Installation
docs.text:
make check

You should see all checks pass.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Verilator not found

Ensure verilator is in your PATH. Add to ~/.bashrc if needed: 

export PATH=/usr/local/bin:$PATH

Permission errors

Use pip install --user or a virtual environment if you encounter permission issues.

docs.title: RTL Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for the Open AXI Interconnect RTL modules.

docs.title: Module Hierarchy
docs.text:
axi_subsystem (top)
├── axi_lite_interconnect
│   └── Address decode + route to 4 slaves
├── ram
│   └── 4 KB memory array + control registers
├── uart
│   └── TX/RX data + control/status registers
├── timer
│   └── Counter, compare, and IRQ generation
└── gpio
    └── 32-pin tristate GPIO with direction/output/input registers

docs.title: Module Summary
docs.text: Module File Description axi_subsystem rtl/top/axi_subsystem.sv Top-level wrapper axi_lite_interconnect rtl/axi/axi_lite_interconnect.sv Address decode & routing axi_lite_slave rtl/axi/axi_lite_slave.sv Generic AXI4-Lite register slave ram rtl/peripherals/ram.sv 4 KB memory with AXI4-Lite interface uart rtl/peripherals/uart.sv Minimal UART peripheral timer rtl/peripherals/timer.sv Timer with compare match IRQ gpio rtl/peripherals/gpio.sv 32-bit bidirectional GPIO

docs.title: Parameterization
docs.text:
All modules use Verilog parameters for configurability:

Parameter Default Description ADDR_WIDTH 32 AXI address bus width DATA_WIDTH 32 AXI data bus width

Peripherals have additional parameters (e.g., NUM_PINS for GPIO).

docs.title: Interface Convention
docs.text:
All modules expose a standard AXI4-Lite slave interface with the following channels:

  • Write Address (AW): awaddr, awvalid, awready
  • Write Data (W): wdata, wstrb, wvalid, wready
  • Write Response (B): bresp, bvalid, bready
  • Read Address (AR): araddr, arvalid, arready
  • Read Data (R): rdata, rresp, rvalid, rready

See AXI Protocol for timing diagrams and protocol details.

docs.title: Top-Level Module — axi_subsystem
docs.text: The axi_subsystem module is the top-level wrapper that instantiates the AXI4-Lite interconnect and all peripherals.

docs.title: File
docs.text: rtl/top/axi_subsystem.sv

docs.title: Instantiation Diagram
docs.text:
┌─────────────────┐
   AXI4-Lite    ───►│  axi_subsystem  │───► AXI4-Lite to RAM
   Master           │                 │───► AXI4-Lite to UART
   (single master)  │  ┌───────────┐  │───► AXI4-Lite to TIMER
                    │  │interconnect│  │───► AXI4-Lite to GPIO
                    │  └───────────┘  │
                    │      │          │
                    │   ┌──┴──┐       │
                    │   ▼     ▼       │
                    │  RAM  UART      │
                    │ TIMER GPIO      │
                    └─────────────────┘

docs.title: Ports
docs.text: Port Direction Width Description clk Input 1 Global clock rst_n Input 1 Active-low reset uart_tx Output 1 UART transmit line uart_rx Input 1 UART receive line timer_irq Output 1 Timer interrupt request gpio_pins Inout 32 Bidirectional GPIO pins

docs.title: AXI4-Lite Master Interface
docs.text: The subsystem exposes a single AXI4-Lite master interface (from the interconnect's perspective, this is the master port). All AXI4-Lite signals are exposed at the top level for connection to an external CPU or bus master.

docs.title: Peripheral Base Addresses
docs.text:
Peripheral Base Address Size RAM 0x0000_0000 4 KB UART 0x4000_0000 4 KB Timer 0x4001_0000 4 KB GPIO 0x4002_0000 4 KB

See Memory Map for full details.

docs.title: Integration Example
docs.text:
axi_subsystem u_subsystem (
    .clk       (sys_clk),
    .rst_n     (sys_rst_n),
    .uart_tx   (uart_tx),
    .uart_rx   (uart_rx),
    .timer_irq (timer_irq),
    .gpio_pins (gpio_pins),

    // AXI4-Lite master interface
    .awaddr    (cpu_awaddr),
    .awvalid   (cpu_awvalid),
    .awready   (cpu_awready),
    // ... (other AXI signals)
);

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: The Open AXI Interconnect includes a comprehensive verification environment built with cocotb and Verilator.

docs.title: Testbench Architecture
docs.text:
tb/
├── axi_interconnect_tb.sv      # SystemVerilog DUT wrapper
├── tests/
│   ├── test_basic_transfer.py  # Single-beat read/write
│   ├── test_burst_transfer.py  # Burst transactions
│   ├── test_concurrent.py      # Concurrent master access
│   ├── test_arbitration.py     # Arbiter behavior
│   └── test_protocol.py        # Protocol compliance
└── models/
    ├── axi_master_bfm.py       # Master bus functional model
    └── axi_slave_bfm.py        # Slave bus functional model

docs.title: All Tests
docs.text: make test

docs.title: Specific Test
docs.text: pytest tb/tests/test_basic_transfer.py -v

docs.title: With Coverage
docs.text: make test COVERAGE=1

docs.title: Test Categories
docs.text: Category Tests Description Basic test_basic_transfer Single read/write transactions Burst test_burst_transfer INCR, WRAP, FIXED burst types Concurrent test_concurrent Multiple masters active simultaneously Arbitration test_arbitration Round-robin and priority arbitration Protocol test_protocol AXI protocol compliance checks

docs.text: Metric Target Status Line Coverage 95%  Achieved Branch Coverage 90%  Achieved Toggle Coverage 90%  In Progress FSM Coverage 100%  Achieved

docs.text:
